{{Orphan|date=November 2024}}

[[File:MEMS Microcantilever in Resonance.png|thumb|Mems microcantilever in resonance]]
'''Anchor losses''' are a type of [[damping]] commonly highlighted in [[Microelectromechanical system oscillator|micro-resonators]]. They refer to the phenomenon where energy is dissipated as mechanical waves from the resonator attenuate into the substrate.

== Introduction ==
In [[physical system]]s, damping is the loss of [[energy]] of an [[oscillating system]] by [[dissipation]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Escudier |first1=Marcel |last2=Atkins |first2=Tony |date=2019 |title=A Dictionary of Mechanical Engineering |website=Oxford Reference |doi=10.1093/acref/9780198832102.001.0001|isbn=978-0-19-883210-2 }}</ref> In the field of micro-electro-mechanicals, the damping is usually measured by a dimensionless parameter [[Q factor]] (Quality factor). A higher Q factor indicates lower damping and reduced energy dissipation, which is desirable for micro-resonators as it leads to lower energy consumption, better accuracy and efficiency, and reduced noise.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Piazza |first1=Gianluca |last2=Stephanou |first2=Philip J. |last3=Pisano |first3=Albert P. |date=2006 |title=Piezoelectric Aluminum Nitride Vibrating Contour-Mode MEMS Resonators |journal=Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems |volume=15 |issue=6 |pages=1406–1418 |doi=10.1109/JMEMS.2006.886012 |issn=1057-7157}}</ref>

Several factors contribute to the damping of micro-electro-mechanical resonators, including fluid damping and solid damping.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |first1=Alberto |last1=Corigliano |first2=Raffaele |last2=Ardito |first3=Claudia |last3=Comi |first4=Attilio |last4=Frangi |first5=Aldo |last5=Ghisi |first6=Stefano |last6=Mariani |title=Mechanics of microsystems |date=2017 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons}}</ref> Anchor losses are a type of solid damping observed in resonators operating in various environments. When a resonator is fixed to a substrate, either directly or via other structures such as tethers, [[mechanical wave]]s propagate into the substrate through these connections. The wave traveling through a perfectly elastic solid would have a constant energy and an isolated perfectly elastic solid once set into vibration would continue to vibrate indefinitely. Actual materials do not show such behavior and dissipation will happen due to some imperfection of elasticity within the body.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Knopoff |first1=Leon |last2=MacDonald |first2=Gordon J. F. |date=1958-10-01 |title=Attenuation of Small Amplitude Stress Waves in Solids |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.30.1178 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=30 |issue=4 |pages=1178–1192 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.30.1178|bibcode=1958RvMP...30.1178K |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In typical micro-resonators, the substrate dimensions are significantly larger than those of the resonator itself. Consequently, it can be approximated that all waves entering the substrate will attenuate without reflecting back to the resonator. In other words, the energy carried by the waves will dissipate, leading to damping. This phenomenon is referred to as anchor losses.

== Estimation of anchor losses ==

=== Analytical estimation ===
Standard theories of structural mechanics permit the expression of concentrated forces and couples exerted by the structure on the support. These generally include a constant component (due, for instance, to pre-stresses or initial deformation) and a sinusoidal varying contribution.<ref name=":0" /> Some researchers have investigated some simple geometries following this idea,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1954-05-20 |title=The field and radiation impedance of mechanical radiators on the free surface of a semi-infinite isotropic solid |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rspa.1954.0134 |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences |language=en |volume=223 |issue=1155 |pages=521–541 |doi=10.1098/rspa.1954.0134 |bibcode=1954RSPSA.223..521M |issn=0080-4630 |last1=Miller |first1=G. F. |last2=Pursey |first2=H. |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=1956-01-05 |title=Forced vibrations of a rigid circular plate on a semi-infinite elastic space and on an elastic stratum |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsta.1956.0001 |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences |language=en |volume=248 |issue=948 |pages=327–368 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1956.0001 |bibcode=1956RSPTA.248..327B |issn=0080-4614 |last1=Bycroft |first1=G. N. |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Judge |first1=John A. |last2=Photiadis |first2=Douglas M. |last3=Vignola |first3=Joseph F. |last4=Houston |first4=Brian H. |last5=Jarzynski |first5=Jacek |date=2007-01-01 |title=Attachment loss of micromechanical and nanomechanical resonators in the limits of thick and thin support structures |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |volume=101 |issue=1 |pages=013521–013521–11 |doi=10.1063/1.2401271 |bibcode=2007JAP...101a3521J |issn=0021-8979}}</ref> and one example is the anchor losses of a cantilever beam connected to a 3-D semi-infinite region:

<math>Q_{anchor}\approx C \left ( \frac{L}{W} \right )\left ( \frac{L}{H} \right )^4</math>

where L is the length of the beam, H is the in-plane (curvature plane) thickness, W is the out-of-plane thickness, C is a constant depending on the Poisson's coefficient, with C = 3.45 for ν = 0.25, C = 3.23 for ν = 0.3, C = 3.175 for ν = 0.33.

=== Numerical estimation ===
{{Main|Perfectly matched layer}}
[[File:Numerical simulation of wave attenuation in a substrate induced by a cantilever beam with surrounding PMLs.gif|thumb|Numerical simulation of wave attenuation in a substrate induced by a cantilever beam with surrounding PMLs]]Due to the complexity of geometries and the anisotropy or inhomogeneities of materials, usually it is difficult to use analytical method to estimate the anchor losses of some devices. Numerical methods are more widely applied for this issue. An artificial boundary or an artificial absorbing layer is applied to the numerical model to prevent the wave reflection. One such method is the [[perfectly matched layer]], initially developed for electromagnetic wave transmission and later adapted for solid mechanics. Perfectly matched layers act as special elements where wave attenuation occurs through a complex coordinate transformation, ensuring all waves entering the layer are absorbed, thus simulating anchor losses.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bindel |first1=David S. |last2=Govindjee |first2=Sanjay |date=2005-10-14 |title=Elastic PMLs for resonator anchor loss simulation |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/nme.1394 |journal=International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering |language=en |volume=64 |issue=6 |pages=789–818 |doi=10.1002/nme.1394 |bibcode=2005IJNME..64..789B |issn=0029-5981|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Frangi |first1=A. |last2=Bugada |first2=A. |last3=Martello |first3=M. |last4=Savadkoohi |first4=P.T. |date=2013 |title=Validation of PML-based models for the evaluation of anchor dissipation in MEMS resonators |journal=European Journal of Mechanics - A/Solids |volume=37 |pages=256–265 |doi=10.1016/j.euromechsol.2012.06.008 |bibcode=2013EuJMA..37..256F |issn=0997-7538}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Peng |last2=Ou |first2=Jun-Yu |last3=Yan |first3=Jize |date=2022 |title=Method for optimising the performance of PML in anchor-loss limited model via COMSOL |journal=IET Science, Measurement & Technology |language=en |volume=16 |issue=6 |pages=327–336 |doi=10.1049/smt2.12107 |issn=1751-8822|doi-access=free }}</ref>

To determine the Q factor from a Finite Element Method model with perfectly matched layers, two common approaches are used:

* Using the complex eigenfrequency from a modal analysis:

<math>Q=\frac{Re(\omega)}{2Im(\omega)}</math>

where <math display="inline">Re(\omega)</math> and <math display="inline">Im(\omega)</math> is the real and imaginary part of the complex eigenfrequency.<ref name=":0" />

* Generating the frequency response from a frequency domain analysis and applying methods such as the half-bandwidth method to calculate the Q factor.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Manzaneque |first1=T. |last2=Hernando |first2=J. |last3=Rodríguez-Aragón |first3=J. |last4=Ababneh |first4=A. |last5=Seidel |first5=H. |last6=Schmid |first6=U. |last7=Sánchez-Rojas |first7=J. L. |title=Smart Sensors, Actuators, and MEMS IV |chapter=Analysis of the quality factor of piezoelectric-actuated micro-resonators |date=2009 |editor-last=Schmid |editor-first=Ulrich  |chapter-url=http://proceedings.spiedigitallibrary.org/proceeding.aspx?doi=10.1117/12.821651 |series=Proceedings of the SPIE  |volume=7362 |pages=73620A |doi=10.1117/12.821651|bibcode=2009SPIE.7362E..0AM |chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>
[[File:Different tether designs for a capacitive resonator.jpg|thumb|Different tether configurations for a capacitive resonator]]

== Methods to mitigate anchor losses ==
Anchor losses are highly dependent on the geometry of the resonator. How to anchor the resonator or the size of the tether has a strong effect on the anchor losses. Some common methods to eliminate anchor losses are summarized as followings.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wu |first1=Guoqiang |last2=Xu |first2=Jinghui |last3=Ng |first3=Eldwin Jiaqiang |last4=Chen |first4=Wen |date=2020 |title=MEMS Resonators for Frequency Reference and Timing Applications |journal=Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems |volume=29 |issue=5 |pages=1137–1166 |doi=10.1109/JMEMS.2020.3020787 |bibcode=2020JMemS..29.1137W |issn=1057-7157}}</ref>

=== Anchor at nodal points ===
A common method is to fix the resonator at the [[Standing wave|nodal points]], where the motion amplitude is minimum.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Sheng-Shian Li |last2=Yu-Wei Lin |last3=Yuan Xie |last4=Zeying Ren |last5=Nguyen |first5=C.T.-C. |chapter=Micromechanical "hollow-disk" ring resonators |date=2004 |title=17th IEEE International Conference on Micro Electro Mechanical Systems. Maastricht MEMS 2004 Technical Digest |publisher=IEEE |pages=821–824 |doi=10.1109/MEMS.2004.1290711 |isbn=978-0-7803-8265-7}}</ref> From the definitions of anchor losses, now the wave magnitude into the substrate will be minimized and less energy will dissipate. However, this method may not apply to certain resonators, in which the nodal points are not around the resonator edges, causing difficulty in tether designs.

=== Quarter wavelength tethers ===
Quarter [[wavelength]] tether is an effective approach to minimize the energy loss through these tethers. Similar to the theory used for transmission lines, quarter wavelength tether is assumed as the best acoustic isolation, since the complete in phase reflection occurs as the tether length equals to a quarter acoustic wavelength, or λ/4. Therefore, there is hardly any energy dissipation to the substrate through the tethers. However, quarter-wavelength design results in extremely long tether structures, usually in tens to hundreds of micrometers, which is counter to minimization and leads to a decrease in the mechanical stability of the devices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kun Wang |last2=Ark-Chew Wong |last3=Nguyen |first3=C.T.-C. |date=2000 |title=VHF free-free beam high-Q micromechanical resonators |journal=Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=347–360 |doi=10.1109/84.870061 |issn=1057-7157}}</ref>

=== Material-mismatched support ===
The resonator structure and anchoring stem are made with different materials. The acoustic impedance mismatch between these two suppresses the energy from the resonator to the stem, thus reducing anchor losses and allowing high Q factor.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Newell |first=W.E. |date=1965 |title=Face-mounted piezoelectric resonators |journal=Proceedings of the IEEE |volume=53 |issue=6 |pages=575–581 |doi=10.1109/PROC.1965.3925 |issn=0018-9219}}</ref>

=== Acoustic reflection cavity ===
The basic mechanism is to reflect back a portion of the elastic waves at the anchor boundary due to the discontinuity in the acoustic impedance caused by the acoustic cavity (the etching trenches).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Harrington |first1=B P |last2=Abdolvand |first2=R |date=2011-08-01 |title=In-plane acoustic reflectors for reducing effective anchor loss in lateral–extensional MEMS resonators |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0960-1317/21/8/085021 |journal=Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering |volume=21 |issue=8 |article-number=085021 |doi=10.1088/0960-1317/21/8/085021 |bibcode=2011JMiMi..21h5021H |issn=0960-1317|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Phonon crystal tether and metamaterial ===
Phonon crystal tether is a promising way to restrain the acoustic wave propagation in the supporting tethers, since they can arouse complete band gaps in which the transmissions of the elastic waves are prohibited. Thus, the vibration energy is retained in the resonator body, reducing the anchor losses into the substrate.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=GHz spurious mode free AlN lamb wave resonator with high figure of merit using one dimensional phononic crystal tethers |url=https://pubs.aip.org/apl/article/109/1/013506/31201/GHz-spurious-mode-free-AlN-lamb-wave-resonator |access-date=2024-07-11 |journal=Applied Physics Letters |date=2016 |doi=10.1063/1.4955410 |last1=Wu |first1=Guoqiang |last2=Zhu |first2=Yao |last3=Merugu |first3=Srinivas |last4=Wang |first4=Nan |last5=Sun |first5=Chengliang |last6=Gu |first6=Yuandong |volume=109 |issue=1 |page=013506 |bibcode=2016ApPhL.109a3506W |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Besides the phonon crystal tether, some other kinds of [[metamaterial]] could be applied to the anchor and surrounding regions to prohibit the wave transmission.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Lixia |last2=Zhu |first2=Chuang |last3=Liu |first3=Haixia |last4=Li |first4=Yan |last5=Wang |first5=Qi |last6=Su |first6=Kun |date=2022 |title=Quality Factor Enhancement of Piezoelectric MEMS Resonator Using a Small Cross-Section Connection Phononic Crystal |journal=Sensors |language=en |volume=22 |issue=20 |page=7751 |doi=10.3390/s22207751 |issn=1424-8220 |pmc=9609283 |pmid=36298102 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2022Senso..22.7751L }}</ref> A key drawback of this method is the challenge to the fabrication process.

=== Optimized anchor geometry ===
Anchor losses are highly sensitive to the geometry of the anchors. Features such as fillets, curvature, sidewall inclination, and other detailed geometric aspects can affect anchor losses. By carefully optimizing these geometric configurations, anchor losses can be significantly reduced.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siddiqi |first1=Muhammad Wajih Ullah |last2=Fedeli |first2=Patrick |last3=Tu |first3=Cheng |last4=Frangi |first4=Attilio |last5=Lee |first5=Joshua E-Y |date=2019-10-01 |title=Numerical analysis of anchor loss and thermoelastic damping in piezoelectric AlN-on-Si Lamb wave resonators |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1361-6439/ab392c |journal=Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering |volume=29 |issue=10 |page=105013 |doi=10.1088/1361-6439/ab392c |bibcode=2019JMiMi..29j5013S |issn=0960-1317|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Segovia-Fernandez |first1=Jeronimo |last2=Cremonesi |first2=Massimiliano |last3=Cassella |first3=Cristian |last4=Frangi |first4=Attilio |last5=Piazza |first5=Gianluca |date=2015 |title=Anchor Losses in AlN Contour Mode Resonators |journal=Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=265–275 |doi=10.1109/JMEMS.2014.2367418 |bibcode=2015JMemS..24..265S |issn=1057-7157}}</ref>
